result.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the diff shows `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` followed by `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal is always a non-empty string, so the `||` fallback can never fire and the `unable_to_add_guests` locale key added in this same diff is unreachable — the intended fallback (e.g., when err.message is empty) will never display, and the toast would instead show something like 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR: '. adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always returns a string, so `message` will be truthy even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (e.g. it becomes `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is unreachable and users may see an unhelpful `undefined:` prefix instead of the intended generic error.
